2. Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
It is the case of the petitioners that the petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 and 3 are the sons of the deceased Aleem Ulla Sharif @ Alim Sharif who died in the Road Traffic Accident on 28.09.2022 due to the negligence of the driver of the respondent's lorry.

It is submitted that on 28.09.2022 at about 10.30 p.m., deceased Aleem Ulla Sharif @ Alim Sharif was riding a bicycle on extreme left side of the road at Bharath Petrol bunk, Mysore road, near BGS flyover, Bengaluru, at that time, the respondent's Cement Mixture Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AC-3862 came with high speed in a rash and SCCH 15 4 MVC No.5656/2022 negligent manner and dashed against the Aleem Sharif resulting in the accident.
As a result of the collision, the deceased sustained fatal injuries and died on the spot.

Rizwan Banu vs Sunil B.S on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132437983/
2 3.

Consequently, on 29.09.2022 FIR No.0080/2022 was registered with the Chickpet Traffic Police station under Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC and charge sheet was filed under Sec.279, 304(A) of IPC and under Sec.3(1), 181, 5(1) and 180 of IMV Act against the driver of the offending vehicle.
4.
The Petitioners submit that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver lorry.

It is submitted that the deceased was hale and healthy and aged about 52 years and working as coolie and was earning Rs.25,000/- p.m. at the time of accident and he was the sole bread earner and had good future prospects.
Due to untimely death of the deceased the Petitioners have lost love, affection and support which has caused mental agony to the petitioners.

Hence, the petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with costs and interest at the rate of 12%
p.a in SCCH 15 5 MVC No.5656/2022 the interest of justice and equity.
5. In pursuance of service of notice issued to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 has remained absent and he was placed exparte.

Respondent No.2 filed Written Statement contending as follows:
The respondent No.2 denies that it has issued insurance policy to the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AC-3862 in favour of the respondent No.1.
Without prejudice the liability of the respondent No.2 if any is subject to the validity of driving license and terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
The driver of the said lorry did not have valid and effective driving license.
It is denied that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry.

The age,
avocation and income of the deceased is denied.
The petition is bad for non joinder of the necessary parties.
Hence, on these grounds Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

SCCH 15 6 MVC No.5656/2022 6. Vide order dated 20.12.2023 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that Aleem Ulla Sharif @ Alim Sharif S/o Late Mohammed Nabedar was died in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred 28.09.2022 at about 10.30 p.m., near Mysore road, Opposite Bharath Petrol bunk, Chamarajpet,
Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Cement Mixture Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA- 01-AC-3862?
2) Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Aleem Ulla Sharif @ Alim Sharif?

Having heard the arguments and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative SCCH 15 8 MVC No.5656/2022 Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.4 : As per the Final Order for the following :
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:
Before adjudication of the issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the issue of negligence.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the rash and negligent driving of driver of Cement Mixture Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AC-3862 (herein after referred to as offending vehicle) caused the accident resulting in the death of Aleem Ulla Sharif.

11. In order to substantiate the same has deposed that on 28.09.2022 at about 10.30 p.m. the deceased was riding bicycle on extreme left side of the road on Mysore road, near B.B. Down, Bapuji nagar and when he reached near BGS flyover at that time Cement Mixture lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AC-3862 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed him and he died on the spot.
SCCH 15 9 MVC No.5656/2022 Rizwan Banu vs Sunil B.S on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132437983/
4 12.

In support of the same PW.1 has produced Ex.P1 FIR which discloses that case has been registered against the driver of the cement mixture lorry for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 304A of IPC and Ex.P2 is the Complaint and Ex.P3 and 4 are the Spot mahazar and Sketch which shows the spot of the accident to be somewhere at the side of the road and after investigation officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences under Sec.279 and 304A of IPC and under Sec.3(1), 181, 5(1) and 180 of IMV Act.

As far as the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle is concerned PW.1 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 wherein PW.1 has admitted that the accident took place at the time of getting down from the flyover.
Except the said suggestion nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 to prove the negligence on the part of the deceased.
The respondent No2 has taken a contention that some other vehicle was caused the accident and the insured vehicle of respondent no 2 is falsely implicated in this case.
SCCH 15 10 MVC No.5656/2022 However nothing is placed on record to show involvement of some other vehicle or collusion of any kind in falsely implicating the offending vehicle.

On the other hand the petitioners have got examined PW.2 and 3 who have also deposed that they are eye witnesses and witnessed the accident and deposed that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Hence, in the absence of any rebuttal evidence on the basis of the evidence of PW.1 to 3 coupled with the documentary evidence it is concluded the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 "in the Affirmative".
13. Issue No.2: It is stated in the Petition as well as in the evidence of PW.1 that the Petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 and 3 are the sons of the deceased Aleem Sharif.
To prove their relationship with the deceased, PW.1 has relied on Ex.P8 to 11 i.e., the Aadhaar cards of the deceased and petitioners.

In the case of Seema Rani & Ors. v. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors 2025 the Supreme Court reiterated that the major, married, and earning children of a deceased victim, as the legal representatives, have the right to apply for motor accident compensation.

entities.text: Seema Rani & Ors. v. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors 2025
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reliance can also be placed on the dictum in National Insurance Company Limited v. Birender (2020), wherein it was expounded that "major married and earning sons of the deceased, being legal representatives, have a right to apply for compensation, and the Tribunal must consider the application, irrespective of whether the representatives are fully dependent on the deceased or not."

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Birender (2020)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
15. Though the Petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 and 3 are the sons of the deceased,
being the legal representatives of deceased Aleem Ulla Sharif @ Alim Sharif have a right to apply for compensation.

As the Petitioners are the LRs of deceased Aleem Ulla Sharif @ Alim Sharif and also they have proved that the death of Aleem Ulla Sharif @ Alim Sharif has been caused by the rash and negligent driving of the SCCH 15 12 MVC No.5656/2022 driver of the offending vehicle, they are entitled for the compensation.
Hence I answer Issue No 2 in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.3

: Computation of compensation under the various heads is assessed as follows:
1. Loss of dependency Age factor:
In order to assess the compensation under the head of loss of dependency the age, avocation and income of the deceased needs to be ascertained.
In the present case, the age of the deceased is shown as 52 years.
Ex.P-9 is the Aadhaar card which shows that the date of birth of the deceased is 01.01.1970.
The alleged accident has taken place on 28.09.2022.

Hence, by considering Ex.P9,
the age of the deceased is taken as 53 years.
17. Income and avocation:
It is stated in the evidence that deceased was working as a coolie and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
The Petitioners have not produced any documentary evidence to prove the actual income of the SCCH 15 13 MVC No.5656/2022 deceased.
Hence in the absence of evidence to prove the actual income of the deceased the notional income will have to be taken into consideration.
Looking into the age of the deceased and the avocation it is just and proper to fix the notional income of the deceased as Rs.15,500/- per month.
Therefore, the Annual Income of the deceased would be 15,500X 12= 1,86,000/-.
Hence for the purpose of computation of claim, the annual income of the deceased is taken as Rs.1,86,000/-.
18. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Sarla Verma v. DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121 has established the golden principles in considering compensation in cases of death.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Relevant part of the judgment at paras 18- 19 is reproduced hereunder:
"18.

The criteria which are to be taken into consideration for assessing compensation in the case of death are: (i) the age of the deceased at the time of his death; (ii) the number of dependents left behind by the deceased; and (iii) the income of the deceased at the time of his death.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:

sentences.text: "Step 1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance, which is considered to be the contribution to the dependant family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step 2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a Table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said Table with SCCH 15 15 MVC No.5656/2022 reference to the age of the deceased."

Moving forward with the Point of future prospects, the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi reported as (2017) 16 SCC 680, held that Future prospects are to be awarded on the basis of:
(i) The nature of the deceased's employment; and (ii) The age of the deceased.
Relying on Para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi (supra), while determining the income, an addition of 10% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects should be made, where the deceased is self - employed and was between the age of 50 to 60 years.
19.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi reported as (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At the time of the death of the deceased, he was survived by his wife and sons.
Hence while calculating the deductions towards the personal expenses, the number of dependents at the time of the death of the deceased is to be considered.

As per the dicta of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India where the number of dependents of family members is 2 SCCH 15 16 MVC No.5656/2022 to 3, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
20.
In this Petition, the deceased was aged 53 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 10% of the income has to be added.
So, 10% of Rs.15,500/- comes to Rs.1,550/-.

Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.17,050/- p.m. (Rs.15,500/- + Rs.1,550/- =
Rs.17,050/-).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 11.

entities.text: (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has pleased to hold that where the number of dependent of family members is 2 to 3, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
21. After deducting 1/3rd of the income towards his personal expenses in Rs.17,050/- it comes to Rs.11,367/-

22. Medical expenses: The petitioners have not produced any medical bills to show any expenses incurred in the hospital.
Hence the actual medical expenses incurred for the treatment of the deceased or any hospital charges are taken an Nil.
23. 'Loss of Estate', Loss of Consortium' and 'Funeral Expenses'

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi (Supra), the conventional heads, namely, 'Loss of Estate',
Loss of Consortium' and 'Funeral Expenses', amount of compensation is fixed as Rs. 15,000/-,
Rs.40,000/- and Rs. 15,000/-, respectively with an increase of 10% after a period of 3 years.
It is further observed in the aforesaid Judgment amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.

By applying the said observation made in the SCCH 15 18 MVC No.5656/2022 aforesaid case, since, more than 6 years lapsed from the date of Order, the consortium fixed in the said case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Further, the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to Rs.18,150/- each.

In view of the decision in United India Insurance Company Limited Vs Satinder Kaur Alias Satwinder Kaur and Ors. (2021) 11 SCC 780, no compensation is to be granted under the head 'Loss of Love and Affection'.

Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

As far as the liability is concerned the official of respondent No.2 company is examined as RW.1 and the specific SCCH 15 20 MVC No.5656/2022 contention taken is that though the offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.2.
However the driver of the offending vehicle did not have valid DL as on the relevant date of the accident.
In the cross-examination of RW.1 he has deposed that they have issued notice to the insured.
However they have not received any reply whether the driver holds valid driving license.
Respondent No.1 on the other hand in this case has remained exparte and has not contested the claim petition.

In order to prove that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess the DL the respondents have relied upon the Ex.P7 - Sec.133 IMV Act notice issued to the owner of the offending vehicle, wherein as per the reply given by the respondent No.1 to the investigation officer it has been submitted that the driver did not have any driving license and there is no information about the DL of driver of offending vehicle.
Hence, there is violation of the policy conditions.

Though the counsel for petitioner has submitted that the burden is on the respondent to lead evidence to prove absence of DL however the SCCH 15 21 MVC No.5656/2022 investigation officer could not be examined in this case since he could not be secured due to his retirement.
However there is clear evidence in the charge sheet to show that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess valid DL as on the date of the accident.
25. The counsel for the petitioners have also not summoned the driver or owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence since there is breach the policy conditions the respondent No.2 is not liable to indemnify respondent No.1 and respondent No.1 will have to deposit the entire compensation amount.

However taking into consideration the hardship likely to be caused to the petitioners in recovering the amount it is just and appropriate to direct the respondent No 2 insurance company to deposit the compensation amount and to recover the same from the owner/ insurer by applying the principles of pay and recover.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No. 3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
26.

Regarding rate of interest: As far as the rate of interest is concerned the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in SCCH 15 22 MVC No.5656/2022 SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY Rizwan Banu vs Sunil B.S on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132437983/

sentences.text: LIMITED VS. RAJASTAN VS. SMT.

LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808 has held that in case of motor accident claims rate of interest awarded is 6% per annum and the Hon'ble High court has been consistently granting 6% interest in Motor Vehicles Accident Claims and Compensation cases.
Hence the rate of interest is set at 6% per annum in this case.
27. Issue No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation of Rs.16,81,944/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.1 and 2 and under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for SCCH 15 23 MVC No.5656/2022 total compensation of Rs.16,81,944/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.

However, the Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest as stated above within 60 days from the date of the Award and thereafter recover the same from the Respondent No.1 through due process of law.

The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
 1) 70% to the Petitioner No.1  After deposit of the Award amount  SCCH 15 24 MVC No.5656/2022 and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 and 2, 50% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 and 2 by way of E-payment and after their proper identification and the remaining 50% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 and 2 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of their choice.
The entire amount awarded to the Petitioner No.3 shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in her name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank till he attains age of majority.
Further, the natural guardian/mother of the minor Petitioner No.3 is permitted to withdraw the interest on the said Fixed deposit periodically to the best interest of the minor Petitioner.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In the case of Seema Rani & Ors. v. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors 2025 the Supreme Court reiterated that the major, married, and earning children of a deceased victim, as the legal representatives, have the right to apply for motor accident compensation.
In order to assess the compensation under the head of loss of dependency the age, avocation and income of the deceased needs to be ascertained.
In the present case, the age of the deceased is shown as 52 years.
The Petitioners have not produced any documentary evidence to prove the actual income of the SCCH 15 13 MVC No.5656/2022 deceased.
Hence in the absence of evidence to prove the actual income of the deceased the notional income will have to be taken into consideration.
Looking into the age of the deceased and the avocation it is just and proper to fix the notional income of the deceased as Rs.15,500/- per month.
Therefore, the Annual Income of the deceased would be 15,500X 12= 1,86,000/-.
Hence for the purpose of computation of claim, the annual income of the deceased is taken as Rs.1,86,000/-.
The criteria which are to be taken into consideration for assessing compensation in the case of death are: (i) the age of the deceased at the time of his death; (ii) the number of dependents left behind by the deceased; and (iii) the income of the deceased at the time of his death.
It will be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.
19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:

6
Moving forward with the Point of future prospects, the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi reported as (2017) 16 SCC 680, held that Future prospects are to be awarded on the basis of:
(i) The nature of the deceased's employment; and (ii) The age of the deceased.
Relying on Para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi (supra), while determining the income, an addition of 10% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects should be made, where the deceased is self - employed and was between the age of 50 to 60 years.
19.
However the driver of the offending vehicle did not have valid DL as on the relevant date of the accident.
In order to prove that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess the DL the respondents have relied upon the Ex.P7 - Sec.133 IMV Act notice issued to the owner of the offending vehicle, wherein as per the reply given by the respondent No.1 to the investigation officer it has been submitted that the driver did not have any driving license and there is no information about the DL of driver of offending vehicle.
Hence, there is violation of the policy conditions.
Though the counsel for petitioner has submitted that the burden is on the respondent to lead evidence to prove absence of DL however the SCCH 15 21 MVC No.5656/2022 investigation officer could not be examined in this case since he could not be secured due to his retirement.
However there is clear evidence in the charge sheet to show that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess valid DL as on the date of the accident.
Hence since there is breach the policy conditions the respondent No.2 is not liable to indemnify respondent No.1 and respondent No.1 will have to deposit the entire compensation amount.
However taking into consideration the hardship likely to be caused to the petitioners in recovering the amount it is just and appropriate to direct the respondent No 2 insurance company to deposit the compensation amount and to recover the same from the owner/ insurer by applying the principles of pay and recover.

27. Issue No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation of Rs.16,81,944/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.
In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.1 and 2 and under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for SCCH 15 23 MVC No.5656/2022 total compensation of Rs.16,81,944/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest as stated above within 60 days from the date of the Award and thereafter recover the same from the Respondent No.1 through due process of law.
The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
 1) 70% to the Petitioner No.1  After deposit of the Award amount  SCCH 15 24 MVC No.5656/2022 and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 and 2, 50% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 and 2 by way of E-payment and after their proper identification and the remaining 50% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 and 2 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of their choice.
The entire amount awarded to the Petitioner No.3 shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in her name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank till he attains age of majority.
Further, the natural guardian/mother of the minor Petitioner No.3 is permitted to withdraw the interest on the said Fixed deposit periodically to the best interest of the minor Petitioner.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
